items.name: Samsung
items.why: One UI 9 / Galaxy AI upgrades are rolling out this week across a large Galaxy installed base, and Reo shows exceptional intent (438 events, 186 developers, last activity 2026-09-19). Clear new-logo wedge on efficient on-device and cloud multimodal inference as they expand AI features at scale.
items.message:
Hi — noticed Samsung is rolling out One UI 9’s Galaxy AI upgrades across a wide set of Galaxy devices this week. Expanding assistant and multimodal features to that many endpoints usually puts real pressure on latency, power, and serving cost, whether workloads stay on-device or burst to the cloud.

We build Modular MAX, an inference engine teams use to run production models more efficiently across heterogeneous hardware. Given Galaxy AI’s mix of edge and cloud serving, it could be a useful fit for your AI runtime stack.

Would you be open to a 20-minute call this week with the team owning Galaxy AI inference performance to compare notes on throughput and unit economics?

items.name: Shopify
items.why: Tobi’s public critique of low-quality internal AI outputs sits alongside Shopify’s AI-first mandate, and Reo shows very strong engagement (302 events, 88 developers, High intent). Timely new-logo outreach on production-grade inference quality and cost behind Shopify Magic.
items.message:
Hi — saw Tobi’s recent comments on the downside of rushed internal AI adoption and the “slop” problem it creates for teams. That tension—push AI hard while insisting on production quality—usually shows up as pressure on serving latency, evaluation loops, and cost per useful output.

Modular’s MAX inference engine helps teams run LLM workloads with better performance and tighter unit economics, which matters when AI features like merchandising and support copilots become always-on merchant surfaces.

If useful, happy to do a short technical walkthrough this week with whoever owns Shopify Magic inference/serving and share how similar platforms are tightening quality without inflating GPU spend.

items.message:

We build Modular MAX to make production inference faster and more efficient, which is often the constraint when agent features move from demo to default.

Would it make sense to connect this week with the Agentforce/platform infra owners for a brief discussion on serving architecture and cost-per-action as agent volume scales?

items.message:
Hi — saw the report that MIS valued HUMAIN’s AI-focused data-centre contract at roughly $2.3B, on top of your AMD Instinct systems coming online and broader IPO/fund plans. Builds of that scale usually force an early decision on the inference runtime layer—especially if you intend to stay hardware-flexible across NVIDIA and AMD.

Modular MAX is built for high-performance, portable inference so serving efficiency keeps pace as clusters land.

Open to a conversation this week with the team defining HUMAIN’s inference/orchestration stack to discuss how MAX could sit in the new capacity?

items.message:

Modular MAX helps teams serve production LLM/ML workloads more efficiently so AI features can scale with order volume rather than with GPU spend.

items.message:
